# Acceptance Criteria - Elite-style Space Trading and Combat Game

## Document Information

- **Document Type**: Acceptance Criteria
- **Epic**: REQ-001
- **Status**: Draft
- **Version**: 1.0

## Overview

This document defines the acceptance criteria for the Elite-style Space Trading and Combat Game. Each acceptance criterion is expressed in Given/When/Then format to provide verifiable, testable specifications for the functional requirements.

---

## AC-1: Game Initialization

## Derived From
- UC-1: Start New Game
- FR: Functional Requirements

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player starts game with initial resources
  Given the game server is running
  And the player accesses the game URL
  When the game initializes
  Then the player is positioned docked at a station
  And the player has exactly 100 credits
  And the player has a small cargo hold with base capacity
  And the station interface is displayed
  And the game is immediately playable without any manual build steps
```

---

## AC-2: Hyperspace Jump Execution

## Derived From
- UC-2: Navigate Between Star Systems
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully jumps between star systems
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient fuel for the jump
  And at least one other star system exists
  When the player selects a destination system
  And confirms the hyperspace jump
  Then the system consumes the required fuel amount
  And the player undocks from the current station
  And hyperspace jump visual effects are rendered
  And the player arrives in the destination system
  And the player can dock at the station in the new system
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player cannot jump with insufficient fuel
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has insufficient fuel for the selected destination
  When the player attempts to confirm the jump
  Then the system prevents the jump
  And an error message is displayed indicating insufficient fuel
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "If fuel >= required_amount, jump succeeds"
    - "If fuel < required_amount, jump fails"
  bounds:
    - "Fuel consumption >= 0"
    - "Fuel consumption <= current_fuel"
  identity:
    - "At zero distance, fuel consumption = 0"
  idempotency:
    - "Executing the same jump twice (if saved/restored) consumes same fuel"
```

## AC-3: Commodity Purchase with Validation

## Derived From
- UC-3: Trade Commodities at Station
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully purchases commodities
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the station has a commodity market
  And the player has sufficient credits
  And the player has sufficient cargo capacity
  When the player selects a commodity to buy
  And specifies a valid quantity
  And confirms the purchase
  Then the transaction is completed
  And credits are deducted equal to (price × quantity)
  And the commodity is added to cargo
  And remaining cargo capacity is reduced by the quantity
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player cannot purchase with insufficient credits
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has insufficient credits for the desired purchase
  When the player attempts to purchase commodities
  Then the system prevents the purchase
  And an error message is displayed indicating insufficient credits
  And no credits are deducted
  And no cargo is added
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player cannot purchase exceeding cargo capacity
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient credits
  And adding the desired quantity would exceed cargo capacity
  When the player attempts to purchase commodities
  Then the system prevents the purchase
  And an error message is displayed indicating insufficient cargo space
  And no credits are deducted
  And no cargo is added
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "If credits >= cost and cargo_space >= quantity, purchase succeeds"
    - "Credits after purchase = credits_before - (price × quantity)"
    - "Cargo usage after purchase = cargo_before + quantity"
  bounds:
    - "Purchase quantity > 0"
    - "Purchase cost <= player_credits"
    - "Purchase quantity <= remaining_cargo_capacity"
  positivity:
    - "Credits after purchase >= 0"
    - "Cargo after purchase <= cargo_capacity"
  idempotency:
    - "Purchasing the same commodity twice increases holdings proportionally"
```

---

## AC-4: Commodity Sale with Validation

## Derived From
- UC-3: Trade Commodities at Station
- FR: Functional Requirements

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully sells commodities
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player owns at least the specified quantity of a commodity
  When the player selects a commodity to sell
  And specifies a valid quantity
  And confirms the sale
  Then the transaction is completed
  And credits are added equal to (sell_price × quantity)
  And the commodity is removed from cargo
  And remaining cargo capacity is increased by the quantity
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player cannot sell more than owned
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player attempts to sell more of a commodity than owned
  When the player attempts to confirm the sale
  Then the system prevents the sale
  And an error message is displayed indicating insufficient commodity quantity
  And no credits are added
  And no cargo is removed
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "If commodity_owned >= quantity, sale succeeds"
    - "Credits after sale = credits_before + (sell_price × quantity)"
    - "Cargo usage after sale = cargo_before - quantity"
  bounds:
    - "Sale quantity > 0"
    - "Sale quantity <= commodity_owned"
  positivity:
    - "Credits after sale >= 0"
    - "Cargo after sale >= 0"
  idempotency:
    - "Selling the same commodity twice reduces holdings proportionally"
```

## AC-5: Combat Victory

## Derived From
- UC-4: Engage in Ship Combat
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player defeats enemy ship in combat
  Given a pirate encounter has been triggered
  And the player is in open space
  When the combat interface is displayed
  And an enemy ship is spawned with AI behavior
  And the player controls ship movement and fires lasers
  And the player destroys the enemy ship
  Then the player receives rewards (credits, cargo, or progression)
  And combat ends
  And the player can continue their journey
  And ship status reflects any combat damage
```

---

## AC-6: Combat Defeat

## Derived From
- UC-4: Engage in Ship Combat
- FR: Functional Requirements

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player is defeated in combat
  Given a pirate encounter has been triggered
  And the player is in open space
  When the combat interface is displayed
  And the enemy ship destroys the player's ship
  Then the game ends or the player respawns with penalties
  And combat ends
  And appropriate consequences are applied
```

---

## AC-7: Successful Combat Flee

## Derived From
- UC-4: Engage in Ship Combat
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully flees from combat
  Given a pirate encounter has been triggered
  And the player is in open space
  And combat is in progress
  When the player chooses to flee
  And the flee attempt is successful
  Then combat ends
  And the player disengages from the enemy
  And the player can continue their journey
  And ship status reflects any combat damage sustained
```

## AC-8: Ship Upgrade Purchase

## Derived From
- UC-5: Upgrade Ship Modules
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully purchases ship upgrade
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the station offers upgrades
  And the player has sufficient credits for at least one upgrade
  And the selected module is not at maximum level
  When the player accesses the upgrade interface
  And selects an upgrade type
  And confirms the purchase
  Then the credits are deducted equal to the upgrade cost
  And the upgrade level is incremented
  And the ship capability is immediately enhanced
  And the display reflects the new upgrade level
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player cannot purchase upgrade with insufficient credits
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has insufficient credits for the desired upgrade
  When the player attempts to purchase the upgrade
  Then the system prevents the purchase
  And an error message is displayed indicating insufficient credits
  And no credits are deducted
  And the upgrade level remains unchanged
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player cannot purchase upgrade at maximum level
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the selected module is at maximum level
  When the player attempts to purchase the upgrade
  Then the system prevents the purchase
  And a message is displayed indicating maximum level reached
  And no credits are deducted
  And the upgrade level remains unchanged
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "If credits >= upgrade_cost and level < max_level, upgrade succeeds"
    - "Upgrade level increases by 1 with each purchase"
    - "Upgrade cost increases with each level"
  bounds:
    - "Upgrade level >= 0"
    - "Upgrade level <= max_level"
    - "Upgrade cost > 0"
  positivity:
    - "Credits after purchase >= 0"
  identity:
    - "At level 0, base ship capabilities apply"
  idempotency:
    - "Purchasing the same upgrade level twice is not allowed"
```

## AC-9: Game State Save

## Derived From
- UC-6: Save Game State
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully saves game state
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the game is in a playable state
  When the player accesses the save game option
  And the system collects all current game state data
  And the system writes the state to a local file
  Then the save operation is confirmed successful
  And a save file exists on the local filesystem
  And the save file contains complete game state at the moment of saving
  And the player can continue playing from the current state
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Save fails due to file permission error
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the game is in a playable state
  When the player attempts to save the game
  And the system cannot write to the filesystem due to permissions
  Then an error is displayed
  And the save fails
  And no save file is created
  And the player can continue playing from the current state
```

---

## AC-10: Game State Load

## Derived From
- UC-7: Load Game State
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player successfully loads saved game state
  Given the game server is running
  And a valid save file exists on the local filesystem
  And the player has accessed the game URL
  When the player accesses the load game option
  And selects a save file to load
  And the system reads and validates the save file
  Then the game state is restored to the saved values
  And the player is positioned at the saved location
  And all player stats, ship configuration, and progress are restored
  And the game resumes from the saved state
  And the game state exactly matches the state at the time of saving
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Load fails due to corrupt save file
  Given the game server is running
  And a save file exists on the local filesystem
  When the player attempts to load the save file
  And the system detects the save file is invalid or corrupted
  Then an error is displayed
  And the load fails
  And the game state remains unchanged
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Load fails due to missing save file
  Given the game server is running
  When the player attempts to load a save file that no longer exists
  Then an error is displayed
  And the load fails
  And the game state remains unchanged
```

## AC-11: Elite Rating Display

## Derived From
- UC-8: View Elite Rating Progress
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player views current Elite rating
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has earned at least some profit or kills
  When the player accesses the status screen
  Then the current Elite rating is displayed
  And total accumulated profit from trading is displayed
  And total combat kills are displayed
  And the next rating tier and requirements are displayed
  And no game state is modified
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Player views Elite rating with no progress
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has no profit or kills
  When the player accesses the status screen
  Then the starting rating is displayed
  And zero profit is displayed
  And zero kills is displayed
  And the first rating tier requirements are displayed
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "Elite rating never decreases"
    - "Rating increases with accumulated profit and kills"
  bounds:
    - "Elite rating >= 0"
    - "Accumulated profit >= 0"
    - "Combat kills >= 0"
  positivity:
    - "Rating tier >= 0"
    - "Progress toward next tier >= 0"
  identity:
    - "At zero profit and zero kills, rating is at starting tier"
  idempotency:
    - "Viewing the rating multiple times does not change the rating"
```

## AC-12: Commodity Price Display

## Derived From
- UC-3: Trade Commodities at Station
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Player views commodity prices at station
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the station has a commodity market
  When the player accesses the market interface
  Then available commodities are displayed
  And buy prices are displayed for each commodity
  And sell prices are displayed for each commodity
  And prices reflect the current system's economic factors
  And prices remain stable during the session
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "Buy price >= 0"
    - "Sell price >= 0"
    - "Buy price >= sell price (station margin)"
  bounds:
    - "Price variation between systems is sufficient for profitable trading"
    - "Prices remain stable within a system during a single session"
  positivity:
    - "Prices are always positive"
  idempotency:
    - "Viewing prices multiple times shows the same values within a session"
```

---

## AC-13: Pirate Encounter Trigger

## Derived From
- UC-2: Navigate Between Star Systems
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Pirate encounter occurs during hyperspace jump
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient fuel for a jump
  When the player initiates a hyperspace jump
  And the encounter probability calculation triggers a pirate encounter
  Then combat is initiated
  And the player can choose to engage or flee
  And the encounter outcome is deterministic for saved games
```

```gherkin
Scenario: No pirate encounter occurs during hyperspace jump
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has sufficient fuel for a jump
  When the player initiates a hyperspace jump
  And the encounter probability calculation does not trigger a pirate encounter
  Then the player arrives at the destination system without combat
  And the player can dock at the station
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "Encounter probability is between 0 and 1"
    - "Higher probability increases encounter likelihood"
  bounds:
    - "Encounter probability >= 0"
    - "Encounter probability <= 1"
  positivity:
    - "Encounter outcome is binary: occurs or does not occur"
  idempotency:
    - "The same jump always has the same encounter outcome (deterministic)"
```

---

## AC-14: Cargo Capacity Enforcement

## Derived From
- UC-3: Trade Commodities at Station
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: System enforces cargo capacity limits
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player has some cargo in their hold
  And remaining cargo capacity is greater than zero
  When the player attempts to purchase commodities
  And the total after purchase would exceed cargo capacity
  Then the purchase is rejected
  And an error message displays remaining cargo capacity
  And no credits are deducted
  And no cargo is added
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "Total cargo never exceeds cargo capacity"
    - "If (current_cargo + purchase_quantity) > capacity, purchase fails"
  bounds:
    - "Cargo capacity > 0"
    - "Current cargo >= 0"
    - "Current cargo <= cargo capacity"
  positivity:
    - "Remaining cargo capacity >= 0"
  identity:
    - "At zero cargo, remaining capacity = total capacity"
  idempotency:
    - "Cargo capacity only increases through upgrades, not through other means"
```

---

## AC-15: Fuel Tank Upgrade Impact

## Derived From
- UC-5: Upgrade Ship Modules
- FR: Functional Requirements
- RULE: Business Rules

## Acceptance Criterion

```gherkin
Scenario: Fuel tank upgrade increases jump range
  Given the player is docked at a station
  And the player purchases a fuel tank upgrade
  When the upgrade is applied
  Then the maximum fuel capacity increases
  And the player can attempt longer jumps
  And fuel consumption rate may improve
  And the upgrade level is tracked
```

## Properties

```yaml
properties:
  monotonicity:
    - "Fuel tank capacity increases with each upgrade level"
    - "Higher capacity enables longer jumps"
  bounds:
    - "Fuel tank capacity > 0"
    - "Fuel tank capacity <= maximum upgrade level capacity"
  positivity:
    - "Fuel tank capacity is always positive"
  identity:
    - "At base level, fuel tank has minimum capacity"
  idempotency:
    - "Purchasing the same upgrade level twice is not allowed"
```

## Notes

- All acceptance criteria are designed to be verifiable through automated testing or manual verification
- Properties blocks provide mathematical invariants for algorithmic ACs, enabling independent property-based testing
- Each AC traces to at least one UC and one FR/NFR to ensure complete coverage
- RULE artifacts are referenced where they contain enforceable business logic that must be verified
- FR-8 (Visual Rendering System) and FR-9 (Server and Health Endpoint) are verified through NFRs and separate technical acceptance criteria not covered in this document
